branch: S1 FIRES on TWO INDEPENDENT RUNS — all 13 models below the shape-free floor; best significantly below (run A p=0.0078, run B p=0.0310). S3 does not fire.

protocol.prompt: CP14 verbatim, identical for every model, no per-model tuning
protocol.denominators: fixed at 210; parse failures and API errors scored as errors, never dropped
protocol.counts: recomputed from per-structure prediction vectors, not read from stored summary fields

floor_test.verdict: significantly BELOW the floor, not merely short of it

measurement_provenance.defect: the sweep ran TWICE. I launched it with nohup, wrongly concluded from a process check that it had died, and relaunched model-by-model. The first sweep completed at 13:33 and wrote results_original.json (9 models) while the relaunch wrote one m_*.json per model. My aggregation globbed BOTH, so 9 models appeared twice and the table took whichever file the glob ordered last - mixing two independent runs in one leaderboard.
measurement_provenance.run_B: original sweep, 9 models, results_original.json, treated as a REPLICATION

run_to_run_spread.interpretation: the run-to-run spread of K=3 majority voting at temperature 0.7 on this benchmark; any single-run leaderboard position carries roughly +/-0.05, so adjacent rows are NOT separable

unscored.moonshotai/kimi-k2.6: pre-registered; hangs indefinitely (no response on a 2-structure K=1 probe after 10 min) so the failure is the model endpoint not the harness. UNSCORED, not dropped; roster is 13 of a pre-registered 14.

corrections: an earlier version published a leaderboard mixing runs A and B, with 'six model families' in its headline while its own list enumerated EIGHT vendors and its results.json families_covered field held 8 entries. Both are fixed: the leaderboard is single-run (A), the replication is reported separately as a spread estimate, and the vendor count is 8.

an earlier version said 'a 30x parameter range' and 'the largest model tested stays 41 structures below the floor'. Both wrong: they treated the 235B-A22B model as largest when maverick at 400B is larger, and attached the 235B model's 41-structure deficit to it. Range is 50x; the largest model's deficit is 18 and it is TIED FOR BEST. Worse, the same figure plotted a Mistral ladder at 24B/41B - MISTRAL HAS NOT DISCLOSED either model's size, so those figures were invented. The Mistral ladder is removed and all 8 undisclosed-size models are barred from any parameter axis.

largest_model_tested.note: the largest model tested is TIED FOR BEST and still 18 structures short of the floor - the correct and stronger form of the difficulty claim

dense_pair_same_family.note: the SMALLER model wins by 31 structures, six times the 5-structure run-to-run spread

fixed_active_compute_varying_capacity.note: IDENTICAL 17B active parameters; accuracy 43->93 is an EXPERT-COUNT/total-capacity effect at fixed active compute, NOT a compute-scale effect. The earlier text conflated the two axes.

scaling_analysis.conclusion: NO single scaling statement is supported: within a dense family the smaller model wins; at fixed active compute more total capacity helps; across families active parameters carry no signal. What IS supported is the negative claim - across a 50x total-parameter range and every architecture tested, nothing clears the floor.
